# Deep learning

Understand training mechanics, architectures and practical optimization.

## Optional branch

**Goal:** Understand neural networks, backpropagation and practical optimisation.

**Stage checkpoint:** Train a small CPU PyTorch model; compare optimisers, save a checkpoint and explain tensor shapes.

Explore this branch when it helps your goal. Return to the main route at any time; completion is not a gate.

Follow the modules and lessons below at your pace. Finish each exercise, save your evidence and self-assessment, then continue. Completed and Already known count as completed; Skipped is reported separately. You can move ahead at any time.

[Full pipeline](../PIPELINE.md) · [Return to main route: LLM engineering](llm.md)

## Neural network mechanics

<a id="dl-tensors"></a>

### Tensors, shapes, networks and autograd

Explain every dimension and gradient in a small neural network.

**Priority:** Core · **Study:** 2h · **Practice:** 3h

**Prerequisites:** [Linear/logistic regression and gradient descent](ml.md#ml-linear), [Derivatives, chain rule and gradients](math-data.md#math-calculus) Navigation is unrestricted.

#### Concepts

- [ ] **Tensors:** Tensors carry data, dtype and device; shape errors can survive broadcasting and corrupt training.
  - Example: A linear layer maps a (batch, features) tensor to (batch, outputs).
  - Videos:
    - [Tensors for Neural Networks, Clearly Explained!!!](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=L35fFDpwIM4) · StatQuest · Josh Starmer · Focused explanation
      - Explains: A visual, step-by-step explanation of the topic named in the title.
      - Useful because: Use the worked intuition before writing the corresponding small experiment.
      - Watch for: Focus on tensors. Then reproduce the lesson example: A linear layer maps a (batch, features) tensor to (batch, outputs).
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://statquest.org/video_index.html
    - [PyTorch for deep learning — full course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V_xro1bcAuA) · freeCodeCamp · Daniel Bourke · Long course · approximately 26h
      - Explains: Tensors, training workflows, classification, computer vision and model experiments.
      - Useful because: A long hands-on course: study the relevant workflow, then build a small CPU lab.
      - Watch for: Focus on tensors. Then reproduce the lesson example: A linear layer maps a (batch, features) tensor to (batch, outputs).
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/learn-pytorch-for-deep-learning-in-day/
- [ ] **Forward pass:** Layers compose parameterized transformations to produce predictions.
  - Example: A two-layer MLP applies linear, ReLU and linear operations.
  - Videos:
    - [Tensors for Neural Networks, Clearly Explained!!!](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=L35fFDpwIM4) · StatQuest · Josh Starmer · Focused explanation
      - Explains: A visual, step-by-step explanation of the topic named in the title.
      - Useful because: Use the worked intuition before writing the corresponding small experiment.
      - Watch for: Focus on forward pass. Then reproduce the lesson example: A two-layer MLP applies linear, ReLU and linear operations.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://statquest.org/video_index.html
    - [PyTorch for deep learning — full course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V_xro1bcAuA) · freeCodeCamp · Daniel Bourke · Long course · approximately 26h
      - Explains: Tensors, training workflows, classification, computer vision and model experiments.
      - Useful because: A long hands-on course: study the relevant workflow, then build a small CPU lab.
      - Watch for: Focus on forward pass. Then reproduce the lesson example: A two-layer MLP applies linear, ReLU and linear operations.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/learn-pytorch-for-deep-learning-in-day/
- [ ] **Backpropagation and autograd:** Reverse-mode differentiation accumulates gradients through a computation graph; gradients must be cleared between updates.
  - Example: Call optimizer.zero_grad(), loss.backward() and optimizer.step() in order.
  - Videos:
    - [Build micrograd: neural networks and backpropagation](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VMj-3S1tku0) · Andrej Karpathy · From-scratch lecture
      - Explains: A scalar autograd engine, computation graphs and a small neural network.
      - Useful because: Best for understanding what backward() actually does under the surface.
      - Watch for: Focus on backpropagation and autograd. Then reproduce the lesson example: Call optimizer.zero_grad(), loss.backward() and optimizer.step() in order.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://karpathy.ai/zero-to-hero.html
    - [PyTorch for deep learning — full course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V_xro1bcAuA) · freeCodeCamp · Daniel Bourke · Long course · approximately 26h
      - Explains: Tensors, training workflows, classification, computer vision and model experiments.

#### Lab: Tensors, shapes, networks and autograd

Build a two-layer CPU MLP on synthetic data, print layer shapes and compare one autograd derivative with a finite-difference estimate.

**Deliverables**

- Runnable code or notebook with a small reproducible input
- README explaining decisions, results and limitations

**Completion checks**

- [ ] Build a two-layer CPU MLP on synthetic data, print layer shapes and compare one autograd derivative with a finite-difference estimate.
- [ ] Include at least one happy-path and one failure/edge-case check; explain the output using the concept checklist.

#### Ten project recommendations

### Support ticket triage desk

Route incoming support tickets to the right category and show the evidence behind each decision.

**Data:** Generate 120 labeled tickets about login, billing and account setup with fixed seed 42. Label or derive the target: ticket category: login, billing or account setup. Start with a majority-class predictor and keyword rules.

**Output:** A review queue with categories, confidence, evidence and correction controls.

**Effort:** 9h · Beginner → intermediate

- **Tensors, shapes, networks and autograd:** Train a small PyTorch MLP or sequence model using the same target as the baseline. Model target: ticket category: login, billing or account setup; compare with a majority-class predictor and keyword rules. For Tensors, shapes, networks and autograd, explicitly apply Tensors, Forward pass, Backpropagation and autograd.
  - Deliverable: A checkpoint, training curves and a measured ML/DL comparison
  - Check: Explain tensor shapes, activation/loss choice and optimizer; compare validation quality and CPU inference time. Adapt the lesson lab: Build a two-layer CPU MLP on synthetic data, print layer shapes and compare one autograd derivative with a finite-difference estimate.

**Milestones**

- [ ] Define the problem, schema and baseline
- [ ] Tensors, shapes, networks and autograd: A checkpoint, training curves and a measured ML/DL comparison
- [ ] Integrate the components and run acceptance checks
- [ ] Document results and demonstrate to a teammate

**Acceptance**

- [ ] Evaluate 24 held-out tickets and report per-category errors; ambiguous tickets must go to human review.
- [ ] Tensors, shapes, networks and autograd: Explain tensor shapes, activation/loss choice and optimizer; compare validation quality and CPU inference time. Adapt the lesson lab: Build a two-layer CPU MLP on synthetic data, print layer shapes and compare one autograd derivative with a finite-difference estimate.
- [ ] A teammate can reproduce the demo using the README without paid credentials.

**Documentation:** README: purpose, setup, worked example, checks and limitations.

### Sigmoid, tanh, ReLU, GELU and softmax

Choose nonlinearities and interpret multiclass outputs correctly.

**Priority:** Core · **Study:** 2h · **Practice:** 3h

**Prerequisites:** [Tensors, shapes, networks and autograd](dl.md#dl-tensors) Navigation is unrestricted.

#### Concepts

- [ ] **Hidden activations:** Sigmoid/tanh can saturate; ReLU gates negative values; GELU smoothly weights inputs and is common in transformers.
  - Example: Plot values and derivatives for these activations.
  - Videos:
    - [Neural Networks Part 3: ReLU in Action!!!](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=68BZ5f7P94E) · StatQuest · Josh Starmer · Focused explanation
      - Explains: A visual, step-by-step explanation of the topic named in the title.
      - Useful because: Use the worked intuition before writing the corresponding small experiment.
      - Watch for: Focus on hidden activations. Then reproduce the lesson example: Plot values and derivatives for these activations.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://statquest.org/video_index.html
    - [PyTorch for deep learning — full course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V_xro1bcAuA) · freeCodeCamp · Daniel Bourke · Long course · approximately 26h
      - Explains: Tensors, training workflows, classification, computer vision and model experiments.
      - Useful because: A long hands-on course: study the relevant workflow, then build a small CPU lab.
      - Watch for: Focus on hidden activations. Then reproduce the lesson example: Plot values and derivatives for these activations.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/learn-pytorch-for-deep-learning-in-day/
- [ ] **Softmax:** Softmax exponentiates and normalizes logits into probabilities; subtracting the maximum improves numerical stability.
  - Example: Apply softmax to [1000,1001,1002] without overflow.
  - Videos:
    - [Neural Networks Part 5: ArgMax and SoftMax](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KpKog-L9veg) · StatQuest · Josh Starmer · Focused explanation
      - Explains: A visual, step-by-step explanation of the topic named in the title.
      - Useful because: Use the worked intuition before writing the corresponding small experiment.
      - Watch for: Focus on softmax. Then reproduce the lesson example: Apply softmax to [1000,1001,1002] without overflow.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://statquest.org/video_index.html
    - [PyTorch for deep learning — full course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V_xro1bcAuA) · freeCodeCamp · Daniel Bourke · Long course · approximately 26h
      - Explains: Tensors, training workflows, classification, computer vision and model experiments.
      - Useful because: A long hands-on course: study the relevant workflow, then build a small CPU lab.
      - Watch for: Focus on softmax. Then reproduce the lesson example: Apply softmax to [1000,1001,1002] without overflow.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.

- [ ] **Logits versus probabilities:** Logits are unnormalized scores; argmax selects a class and differs from training probabilities.

## Optimization and stability

<a id="dl-optimizers"></a>

### SGD, momentum, RMSprop, Adam and AdamW

Understand what optimizer state changes and why AdamW is different from Adam.

**Priority:** Core · **Study:** 3h · **Practice:** 4h

**Prerequisites:** [MSE, binary and multiclass cross-entropy](dl.md#dl-losses) Navigation is unrestricted.

#### Concepts

- [ ] **SGD and momentum:** SGD follows the current gradient; momentum smooths updates using accumulated direction.
  - Example: Compare zigzagging with and without momentum on an elongated quadratic.
  - Videos:
    - [Adam optimization algorithm](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JXQT_vxqwIs) · DeepLearning.AI · Andrew Ng · Focused lecture
      - Explains: First/second moment estimates, bias correction and Adam updates.
      - Useful because: Work through the optimizer state before comparing Adam with SGD.
      - Watch for: Focus on sgd and momentum. Then reproduce the lesson example: Compare zigzagging with and without momentum on an elongated quadratic.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JXQT_vxqwIs
    - [PyTorch for deep learning — full course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V_xro1bcAuA) · freeCodeCamp · Daniel Bourke · Long course · approximately 26h
      - Explains: Tensors, training workflows, classification, computer vision and model experiments.
      - Useful because: A long hands-on course: study the relevant workflow, then build a small CPU lab.
      - Watch for: Focus on sgd and momentum. Then reproduce the lesson example: Compare zigzagging with and without momentum on an elongated quadratic.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/learn-pytorch-for-deep-learning-in-day/
- [ ] **RMSprop and Adam:** RMSprop rescales by running squared gradients; Adam combines first/second moments with bias correction.
  - Example: Track moment estimates and epsilon during ten manual Adam updates.
  - Videos:
    - [Adam optimization algorithm](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JXQT_vxqwIs) · DeepLearning.AI · Andrew Ng · Focused lecture
      - Explains: First/second moment estimates, bias correction and Adam updates.
      - Useful because: Work through the optimizer state before comparing Adam with SGD.
      - Watch for: Focus on rmsprop and adam. Then reproduce the lesson example: Track moment estimates and epsilon during ten manual Adam updates.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JXQT_vxqwIs
    - [PyTorch for deep learning — full course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V_xro1bcAuA) · freeCodeCamp · Daniel Bourke · Long course · approximately 26h
      - Explains: Tensors, training workflows, classification, computer vision and model experiments.
      - Useful because: A long hands-on course: study the relevant workflow, then build a small CPU lab.
      - Watch for: Focus on rmsprop and adam. Then reproduce the lesson example: Track moment estimates and epsilon during ten manual Adam updates.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/learn-pytorch-for-deep-learning-in-day/
- [ ] **AdamW:** AdamW applies decoupled weight decay instead of mixing the penalty into adaptive gradients.
  - Example: Compare weight norm under Adam and AdamW with otherwise equal settings.
  - Videos:
    - [Adam optimization algorithm](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JXQT_vxqwIs) · DeepLearning.AI · Andrew Ng · Focused lecture
      - Explains: First/second moment estimates, bias correction and Adam updates.
      - Useful because: Work through the optimizer state before comparing Adam with SGD.
      - Watch for: Focus on adamw. Then reproduce the lesson example: Compare weight norm under Adam and AdamW with otherwise equal settings.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JXQT_vxqwIs

      - Explains: Tensors, training workflows, classification, computer vision and model experiments.

      - Watch for: Focus on adamw. Then reproduce the lesson example: Compare weight norm under Adam and AdamW with otherwise equal settings.

      - Verification source: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/learn-pytorch-for-deep-learning-in-day/
- [ ] **Adam update mechanics:** m and v exponentially average gradients and squared gradients using beta1/beta2; divide by 1-beta^t for bias correction, then update with m_hat/(sqrt(v_hat)+epsilon).
  - Example: Calculate the first update for gradient 2, beta1=0.9, beta2=0.999 and compare it with an SGD step.

### Learning rates, schedules, batch sizes and initialization

Make training stable before spending more computation on it.

**Priority:** Core · **Study:** 2h · **Practice:** 3h

**Prerequisites:** [SGD, momentum, RMSprop, Adam and AdamW](dl.md#dl-optimizers) Navigation is unrestricted.

#### Concepts

- [ ] **Learning rates and schedules:** The step size balances speed and stability; warmup and decay can help but must be evaluated.
  - Example: Compare fixed rate with a cosine-decay schedule.
  - Videos:
    - [Improving deep neural networks — complete course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hAbRGXkpTX8) · DeepLearning.AI · Andrew Ng · Full course
      - Explains: Initialization, regularization, gradient checking, optimizers and hyperparameter choices.
      - Useful because: A structured theory companion for optimization and training stability.
      - Watch for: Focus on learning rates and schedules. Then reproduce the lesson example: Compare fixed rate with a cosine-decay schedule.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hAbRGXkpTX8
    - [PyTorch for deep learning — full course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V_xro1bcAuA) · freeCodeCamp · Daniel Bourke · Long course · approximately 26h
      - Explains: Tensors, training workflows, classification, computer vision and model experiments.
      - Useful because: A long hands-on course: study the relevant workflow, then build a small CPU lab.
      - Watch for: Focus on learning rates and schedules. Then reproduce the lesson example: Compare fixed rate with a cosine-decay schedule.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/learn-pytorch-for-deep-learning-in-day/
- [ ] **Batch size:** Batch size changes memory use and gradient noise; gradient accumulation emulates larger updates with smaller physical batches.
  - Example: Accumulate four mini-batches before one optimizer step.
  - Videos:
    - [Improving deep neural networks — complete course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hAbRGXkpTX8) · DeepLearning.AI · Andrew Ng · Full course
      - Explains: Initialization, regularization, gradient checking, optimizers and hyperparameter choices.
      - Useful because: A structured theory companion for optimization and training stability.

      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hAbRGXkpTX8
    - [PyTorch for deep learning — full course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V_xro1bcAuA) · freeCodeCamp · Daniel Bourke · Long course · approximately 26h
      - Explains: Tensors, training workflows, classification, computer vision and model experiments.
      - Useful because: A long hands-on course: study the relevant workflow, then build a small CPU lab.
      - Watch for: Focus on batch size. Then reproduce the lesson example: Accumulate four mini-batches before one optimizer step.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/learn-pytorch-for-deep-learning-in-day/
- [ ] **Initialization:** Xavier/He initialization controls variance through layers; all-zero hidden weights prevent useful symmetry breaking.
  - Example: Inspect activation statistics for zero versus variance-aware initialization.
  - Videos:
    - [Makemore: activations, gradients and BatchNorm](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=P6sfmUTpUmc) · Andrej Karpathy · From-scratch lecture
      - Explains: Activation statistics, initialization problems, gradients and batch normalization.

### Dropout, normalization, clipping and early stopping

Reduce overfitting and prevent unstable updates without contaminating evaluation.

**Priority:** Core · **Study:** 2h · **Practice:** 3h

**Prerequisites:** [Learning rates, schedules, batch sizes and initialization](dl.md#dl-training-settings) Navigation is unrestricted.

#### Concepts

- [ ] **Dropout and weight decay:** Dropout randomly masks activations in training; weight decay shrinks parameters.
  - Example: Use model.eval() so dropout stops changing predictions during validation.
  - Videos:
    - [Makemore: activations, gradients and BatchNorm](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=P6sfmUTpUmc) · Andrej Karpathy · From-scratch lecture
      - Explains: Activation statistics, initialization problems, gradients and batch normalization.
      - Useful because: Debug vanishing/exploding behavior with measured statistics.
      - Watch for: Focus on dropout and weight decay. Then reproduce the lesson example: Use model.eval() so dropout stops changing predictions during validation.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://karpathy.ai/zero-to-hero.html
    - [PyTorch for deep learning — full course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V_xro1bcAuA) · freeCodeCamp · Daniel Bourke · Long course · approximately 26h
      - Explains: Tensors, training workflows, classification, computer vision and model experiments.
      - Useful because: A long hands-on course: study the relevant workflow, then build a small CPU lab.
      - Watch for: Focus on dropout and weight decay. Then reproduce the lesson example: Use model.eval() so dropout stops changing predictions during validation.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/learn-pytorch-for-deep-learning-in-day/
- [ ] **Batch versus layer normalization:** BatchNorm uses batch statistics and running estimates; LayerNorm normalizes within an example and suits variable batches.
  - Example: Compare train/eval outputs for BatchNorm on a tiny batch.
  - Videos:
    - [Makemore: activations, gradients and BatchNorm](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=P6sfmUTpUmc) · Andrej Karpathy · From-scratch lecture
      - Explains: Activation statistics, initialization problems, gradients and batch normalization.
      - Useful because: Debug vanishing/exploding behavior with measured statistics.

    - [PyTorch for deep learning — full course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V_xro1bcAuA) · freeCodeCamp · Daniel Bourke · Long course · approximately 26h
      - Explains: Tensors, training workflows, classification, computer vision and model experiments.
      - Useful because: A long hands-on course: study the relevant workflow, then build a small CPU lab.
      - Watch for: Focus on batch versus layer normalization. Then reproduce the lesson example: Compare train/eval outputs for BatchNorm on a tiny batch.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/learn-pytorch-for-deep-learning-in-day/
- [ ] **Gradient clipping and early stopping:** Clipping bounds gradient norms; early stopping preserves the best validation checkpoint.
  - Example: Stop after several non-improving epochs and restore the best model.

### PyTorch loops, checkpoints and reproducibility

Make a training run inspectable, resumable and comparable.

**Priority:** Core · **Study:** 2h · **Practice:** 3h

**Prerequisites:** [Dropout, normalization, clipping and early stopping](dl.md#dl-regularization) Navigation is unrestricted.

#### Concepts

- [ ] **Training loop:** A loop coordinates data loading, forward pass, loss, gradients and updates; validation should disable gradient recording.
  - Example: Use no_grad or inference_mode and model.eval() for validation.
  - Videos:
    - [PyTorch for deep learning — full course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V_xro1bcAuA) · freeCodeCamp · Daniel Bourke · Long course · approximately 26h
      - Explains: Tensors, training workflows, classification, computer vision and model experiments.
      - Useful because: A long hands-on course: study the relevant workflow, then build a small CPU lab.
      - Watch for: Focus on training loop. Then reproduce the lesson example: Use no_grad or inference_mode and model.eval() for validation.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/learn-pytorch-for-deep-learning-in-day/
- [ ] **Checkpoints:** Save model weights, optimizer state, epoch and configuration to resume a run accurately.
  - Example: Resume at the next epoch with identical scheduler state.
  - Videos:
    - [PyTorch for deep learning — full course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V_xro1bcAuA) · freeCodeCamp · Daniel Bourke · Long course · approximately 26h
      - Explains: Tensors, training workflows, classification, computer vision and model experiments.
      - Useful because: A long hands-on course: study the relevant workflow, then build a small CPU lab.
      - Watch for: Focus on checkpoints. Then reproduce the lesson example: Resume at the next epoch with identical scheduler state.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/learn-pytorch-for-deep-learning-in-day/
- [ ] **Reproducibility:** Seeds help but hardware and kernels may remain nondeterministic; record dependencies and dataset splits.
  - Example: Record the split seed and compare two CPU runs.
  - Videos:
    - [PyTorch for deep learning — full course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V_xro1bcAuA) · freeCodeCamp · Daniel Bourke · Long course · approximately 26h
      - Explains: Tensors, training workflows, classification, computer vision and model experiments.
      - Useful because: A long hands-on course: study the relevant workflow, then build a small CPU lab.
      - Watch for: Focus on reproducibility. Then reproduce the lesson example: Record the split seed and compare two CPU runs.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/learn-pytorch-for-deep-learning-in-day/

**Priority:** Useful next · **Study:** 2h · **Practice:** 3h

- [ ] **Memory accounting:** Parameters, optimizer state, activations and batches all consume memory; training needs more than inference.

## Tensor algebra and differentiation

<a id="dl-shape-algebra"></a>

### Tensor indexing, broadcasting and memory layout

Prevent silent shape mistakes before trusting a model loss or a batch of predictions.

**Priority:** Useful next · **Study:** 3h · **Practice:** 4h

**Prerequisites:** [Tensors, shapes, networks and autograd](dl.md#dl-tensors) Navigation is unrestricted.

#### Concepts

- [ ] **Batch, channel and feature axes:** Name every axis before applying an operation; images and sequences use different layout conventions.
  - Example: Annotate an image batch as N=8, C=3, H=32, W=32 and a token batch as B=8, T=20, D=16.
  - Videos:
    - [Karpathy — Building makemore](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PaCmpygFfXo) · Andrej Karpathy · From-scratch lecture · 1h57m
      - Explains: A character-level bigram language model, tensor operations, likelihood and sampling.
      - Useful because: Reproduce the tiny model locally and inspect shapes and probabilities at each step.
      - Watch for: Focus on batch, channel and feature axes. Then reproduce the lesson example: Annotate an image batch as N=8, C=3, H=32, W=32 and a token batch as B=8, T=20, D=16.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://karpathy.ai/zero-to-hero.html
    - [PyTorch for deep learning — full course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V_xro1bcAuA) · freeCodeCamp · Daniel Bourke · Long course · approximately 26h
      - Explains: Tensors, training workflows, classification, computer vision and model experiments.
      - Useful because: A long hands-on course: study the relevant workflow, then build a small CPU lab.
      - Watch for: Focus on batch, channel and feature axes. Then reproduce the lesson example: Annotate an image batch as N=8, C=3, H=32, W=32 and a token batch as B=8, T=20, D=16.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/learn-pytorch-for-deep-learning-in-day/
- [ ] **Broadcasting from trailing dimensions:** Two aligned dimensions are compatible when equal or one; broadcasting may produce a valid but unintended result.
  - Example: Subtracting targets shaped (32,) from predictions shaped (32,1) produces a (32,32) matrix instead of per-example errors.
  - Videos:
    - [Karpathy — Building makemore](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PaCmpygFfXo) · Andrej Karpathy · From-scratch lecture · 1h57m
      - Explains: A character-level bigram language model, tensor operations, likelihood and sampling.
      - Useful because: Reproduce the tiny model locally and inspect shapes and probabilities at each step.
      - Watch for: Focus on broadcasting from trailing dimensions. Then reproduce the lesson example: Subtracting targets shaped (32,) from predictions shaped (32,1) produces a (32,32) matrix instead of per-example errors.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://karpathy.ai/zero-to-hero.html
    - [PyTorch for deep learning — full course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V_xro1bcAuA) · freeCodeCamp · Daniel Bourke · Long course · approximately 26h
      - Explains: Tensors, training workflows, classification, computer vision and model experiments.
      - Useful because: A long hands-on course: study the relevant workflow, then build a small CPU lab.
      - Watch for: Focus on broadcasting from trailing dimensions. Then reproduce the lesson example: Subtracting targets shaped (32,) from predictions shaped (32,1) produces a (32,32) matrix instead of per-example errors.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/learn-pytorch-for-deep-learning-in-day/
- [ ] **Matrix multiplication versus elementwise multiplication:** The @ operator contracts an inner dimension, while * multiplies matching or broadcast elements.
  - Example: Verify (4,3) @ (3,2) gives (4,2), while (4,3) * (3,) rescales columns.
  - Videos:
    - [Karpathy — Building makemore](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PaCmpygFfXo) · Andrej Karpathy · From-scratch lecture · 1h57m
      - Explains: A character-level bigram language model, tensor operations, likelihood and sampling.
      - Useful because: Reproduce the tiny model locally and inspect shapes and probabilities at each step.
      - Watch for: Focus on matrix multiplication versus elementwise multiplication. Then reproduce the lesson example: Verify (4,3) @ (3,2) gives (4,2), while (4,3) * (3,) rescales columns.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://karpathy.ai/zero-to-hero.html
    - [PyTorch for deep learning — full course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V_xro1bcAuA) · freeCodeCamp · Daniel Bourke · Long course · approximately 26h
      - Explains: Tensors, training workflows, classification, computer vision and model experiments.
      - Useful because: A long hands-on course: study the relevant workflow, then build a small CPU lab.
      - Watch for: Focus on matrix multiplication versus elementwise multiplication. Then reproduce the lesson example: Verify (4,3) @ (3,2) gives (4,2), while (4,3) * (3,) rescales columns.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/learn-pytorch-for-deep-learning-in-day/
- [ ] **Views, reshape and contiguity:** A view shares storage and some views require compatible strides; reshape may allocate a copy.
  - Example: Transpose a matrix, inspect stride(), and compare reshape with contiguous().view().
  - Videos:
    - [Karpathy — Building makemore](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PaCmpygFfXo) · Andrej Karpathy · From-scratch lecture · 1h57m
      - Explains: A character-level bigram language model, tensor operations, likelihood and sampling.
      - Useful because: Reproduce the tiny model locally and inspect shapes and probabilities at each step.
      - Watch for: Focus on views, reshape and contiguity. Then reproduce the lesson example: Transpose a matrix, inspect stride(), and compare reshape with contiguous().view().
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://karpathy.ai/zero-to-hero.html
    - [PyTorch for deep learning — full course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V_xro1bcAuA) · freeCodeCamp · Daniel Bourke · Long course · approximately 26h
      - Explains: Tensors, training workflows, classification, computer vision and model experiments.
      - Useful because: A long hands-on course: study the relevant workflow, then build a small CPU lab.
      - Watch for: Focus on views, reshape and contiguity. Then reproduce the lesson example: Transpose a matrix, inspect stride(), and compare reshape with contiguous().view().
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/learn-pytorch-for-deep-learning-in-day/
- [ ] **Reductions and keepdim:** sum and mean remove selected axes unless keepdim preserves a size-one dimension for broadcasting.
  - Example: Normalise each row with mean(dim=1, keepdim=True) and assert the output shape stays unchanged.
  - Videos:

<a id="dl-gradient-mechanics"></a>

### Gradients, computation graphs and gradient checking

Explain why a parameter receives its gradient and detect broken differentiation in custom computations.

**Priority:** Useful next · **Study:** 3h · **Practice:** 4h

**Prerequisites:** [Tensors, shapes, networks and autograd](dl.md#dl-tensors) Navigation is unrestricted.

#### Concepts

- [ ] **Chain rule along paths:** A parameter influences a loss through many intermediate values; reverse-mode differentiation sums contributions from every path.
  - Example: Differentiate z=x*x+x by hand and compare 2*x+1 with autograd.
  - Videos:
    - [Karpathy — Becoming a Backprop Ninja](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q8SA3rM6ckI) · Andrej Karpathy · From-scratch lecture · 1h55m
      - Explains: Manual tensor-level gradients through an MLP and its normalisation and loss operations.
      - Useful because: Check a small computation by hand and compare its gradients with autograd.
      - Watch for: Focus on chain rule along paths. Then reproduce the lesson example: Differentiate z=x*x+x by hand and compare 2*x+1 with autograd.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://karpathy.ai/zero-to-hero.html
    - [PyTorch for deep learning — full course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V_xro1bcAuA) · freeCodeCamp · Daniel Bourke · Long course · approximately 26h
      - Explains: Tensors, training workflows, classification, computer vision and model experiments.
      - Useful because: A long hands-on course: study the relevant workflow, then build a small CPU lab.
      - Watch for: Focus on chain rule along paths. Then reproduce the lesson example: Differentiate z=x*x+x by hand and compare 2*x+1 with autograd.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/learn-pytorch-for-deep-learning-in-day/
- [ ] **Leaf tensors and gradient accumulation:** Trainable leaf parameters collect .grad values; backward adds to existing gradients rather than replacing them.
  - Example: Run backward twice with fresh forward passes and show how zero_grad changes the result.
  - Videos:
    - [Karpathy — Becoming a Backprop Ninja](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q8SA3rM6ckI) · Andrej Karpathy · From-scratch lecture · 1h55m
      - Explains: Manual tensor-level gradients through an MLP and its normalisation and loss operations.
      - Useful because: Check a small computation by hand and compare its gradients with autograd.
      - Watch for: Focus on leaf tensors and gradient accumulation. Then reproduce the lesson example: Run backward twice with fresh forward passes and show how zero_grad changes the result.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://karpathy.ai/zero-to-hero.html
    - [PyTorch for deep learning — full course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V_xro1bcAuA) · freeCodeCamp · Daniel Bourke · Long course · approximately 26h
      - Explains: Tensors, training workflows, classification, computer vision and model experiments.
      - Useful because: A long hands-on course: study the relevant workflow, then build a small CPU lab.
      - Watch for: Focus on leaf tensors and gradient accumulation. Then reproduce the lesson example: Run backward twice with fresh forward passes and show how zero_grad changes the result.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/learn-pytorch-for-deep-learning-in-day/
- [ ] **Vector-Jacobian products:** Backward propagates a vector through a Jacobian without materialising the full matrix.
  - Example: For y=x*x with several elements, supply an upstream vector and check 2*x*v.
  - Videos:
    - [Karpathy — Becoming a Backprop Ninja](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q8SA3rM6ckI) · Andrej Karpathy · From-scratch lecture · 1h55m
      - Explains: Manual tensor-level gradients through an MLP and its normalisation and loss operations.
      - Useful because: Check a small computation by hand and compare its gradients with autograd.
      - Watch for: Focus on vector-jacobian products. Then reproduce the lesson example: For y=x*x with several elements, supply an upstream vector and check 2*x*v.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://karpathy.ai/zero-to-hero.html
    - [PyTorch for deep learning — full course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V_xro1bcAuA) · freeCodeCamp · Daniel Bourke · Long course · approximately 26h
      - Explains: Tensors, training workflows, classification, computer vision and model experiments.
      - Useful because: A long hands-on course: study the relevant workflow, then build a small CPU lab.
      - Watch for: Focus on vector-jacobian products. Then reproduce the lesson example: For y=x*x with several elements, supply an upstream vector and check 2*x*v.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/learn-pytorch-for-deep-learning-in-day/
- [ ] **Detach and no_grad:** detach breaks graph connectivity and no_grad avoids building a graph; neither is a substitute for switching dropout to evaluation mode.
  - Example: Detach a hidden state intentionally, then explain why detaching the final loss prevents training.
  - Videos:
    - [Karpathy — Becoming a Backprop Ninja](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q8SA3rM6ckI) · Andrej Karpathy · From-scratch lecture · 1h55m
      - Explains: Manual tensor-level gradients through an MLP and its normalisation and loss operations.
      - Useful because: Check a small computation by hand and compare its gradients with autograd.
      - Watch for: Focus on detach and no_grad. Then reproduce the lesson example: Detach a hidden state intentionally, then explain why detaching the final loss prevents training.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://karpathy.ai/zero-to-hero.html
    - [PyTorch for deep learning — full course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V_xro1bcAuA) · freeCodeCamp · Daniel Bourke · Long course · approximately 26h
      - Explains: Tensors, training workflows, classification, computer vision and model experiments.
      - Useful because: A long hands-on course: study the relevant workflow, then build a small CPU lab.
      - Watch for: Focus on detach and no_grad. Then reproduce the lesson example: Detach a hidden state intentionally, then explain why detaching the final loss prevents training.

      - Verification source: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/learn-pytorch-for-deep-learning-in-day/
- [ ] **Finite-difference gradient checks:** A central difference estimates a derivative from nearby loss values; use double precision and avoid nondifferentiable points.
  - Example: Compare (f(w+eps)-f(w-eps))/(2*eps) against autograd for a tiny smooth network.

## Reliable training and optimisation

<a id="dl-initialization-depth"></a>

### Initialisation, signal scale and residual connections

Keep activations and gradients usable as a neural network becomes deeper.

**Priority:** Useful next · **Study:** 3h · **Practice:** 4h

**Prerequisites:** [Sigmoid, tanh, ReLU, GELU and softmax](dl.md#dl-activations) Navigation is unrestricted.

#### Concepts

- [ ] **Symmetry breaking:** Hidden units need different initial weights to learn different features; identical initial units receive identical updates in a symmetric network.
  - Example: Compare two hidden neurons initialised to zero against small random weights.
  - Videos:
    - [Makemore: activations, gradients and BatchNorm](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=P6sfmUTpUmc) · Andrej Karpathy · From-scratch lecture
      - Explains: Activation statistics, initialization problems, gradients and batch normalization.
      - Useful because: Debug vanishing/exploding behavior with measured statistics.
      - Watch for: Focus on symmetry breaking. Then reproduce the lesson example: Compare two hidden neurons initialised to zero against small random weights.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://karpathy.ai/zero-to-hero.html
    - [PyTorch for deep learning — full course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V_xro1bcAuA) · freeCodeCamp · Daniel Bourke · Long course · approximately 26h
      - Explains: Tensors, training workflows, classification, computer vision and model experiments.
      - Useful because: A long hands-on course: study the relevant workflow, then build a small CPU lab.
      - Watch for: Focus on symmetry breaking. Then reproduce the lesson example: Compare two hidden neurons initialised to zero against small random weights.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/learn-pytorch-for-deep-learning-in-day/
- [ ] **Fan-in and fan-out:** The number of incoming and outgoing connections helps determine an initial variance that preserves signal scale.
  - Example: Compute fan-in=64 and fan-out=32 for a linear layer and inspect the initial weight standard deviation.
  - Videos:
    - [Makemore: activations, gradients and BatchNorm](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=P6sfmUTpUmc) · Andrej Karpathy · From-scratch lecture
      - Explains: Activation statistics, initialization problems, gradients and batch normalization.
      - Useful because: Debug vanishing/exploding behavior with measured statistics.
      - Watch for: Focus on fan-in and fan-out. Then reproduce the lesson example: Compute fan-in=64 and fan-out=32 for a linear layer and inspect the initial weight standard deviation.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://karpathy.ai/zero-to-hero.html
    - [PyTorch for deep learning — full course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V_xro1bcAuA) · freeCodeCamp · Daniel Bourke · Long course · approximately 26h
      - Explains: Tensors, training workflows, classification, computer vision and model experiments.
      - Useful because: A long hands-on course: study the relevant workflow, then build a small CPU lab.
      - Watch for: Focus on fan-in and fan-out. Then reproduce the lesson example: Compute fan-in=64 and fan-out=32 for a linear layer and inspect the initial weight standard deviation.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/learn-pytorch-for-deep-learning-in-day/
- [ ] **Xavier versus Kaiming:** Xavier balances input/output scale; Kaiming accounts for rectifying activations and the chosen fan convention.
  - Example: Compare activation variances over six tanh layers and six ReLU layers with suitable initialisers.
  - Videos:
    - [Makemore: activations, gradients and BatchNorm](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=P6sfmUTpUmc) · Andrej Karpathy · From-scratch lecture
      - Explains: Activation statistics, initialization problems, gradients and batch normalization.
      - Useful because: Debug vanishing/exploding behavior with measured statistics.
      - Watch for: Focus on xavier versus kaiming. Then reproduce the lesson example: Compare activation variances over six tanh layers and six ReLU layers with suitable initialisers.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://karpathy.ai/zero-to-hero.html
    - [PyTorch for deep learning — full course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V_xro1bcAuA) · freeCodeCamp · Daniel Bourke · Long course · approximately 26h
      - Explains: Tensors, training workflows, classification, computer vision and model experiments.
      - Useful because: A long hands-on course: study the relevant workflow, then build a small CPU lab.
      - Watch for: Focus on xavier versus kaiming. Then reproduce the lesson example: Compare activation variances over six tanh layers and six ReLU layers with suitable initialisers.

      - Verification source: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/learn-pytorch-for-deep-learning-in-day/
- [ ] **Vanishing and exploding gradients:** Repeated multiplication through depth can shrink or enlarge gradients; inspect norms instead of guessing from the loss alone.
  - Example: Log per-layer gradient norms for a network with deliberately oversized weights.
  - Videos:
    - [Makemore: activations, gradients and BatchNorm](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=P6sfmUTpUmc) · Andrej Karpathy · From-scratch lecture

      - Verification source: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/learn-pytorch-for-deep-learning-in-day/

  - Example: Implement x+F(x), and use a projection when input and output feature dimensions differ.

### Datasets, DataLoader, collation and padding

Build batches that preserve labels, masks and reproducibility rather than hiding data errors inside training.

**Priority:** Useful next · **Study:** 3h · **Practice:** 4h

**Prerequisites:** [PyTorch loops, checkpoints and reproducibility](dl.md#dl-training-loop) Navigation is unrestricted.

#### Concepts

- [ ] **Dataset contract:** A dataset maps an index to a sample and target; test individual items before enabling batch loading.
  - Example: Assert each synthetic image is float32 and its class target is an integer.
  - Videos:
    - [PyTorch for deep learning — full course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V_xro1bcAuA) · freeCodeCamp · Daniel Bourke · Long course · approximately 26h
      - Explains: Tensors, training workflows, classification, computer vision and model experiments.
      - Useful because: A long hands-on course: study the relevant workflow, then build a small CPU lab.
      - Watch for: Focus on dataset contract. Then reproduce the lesson example: Assert each synthetic image is float32 and its class target is an integer.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/learn-pytorch-for-deep-learning-in-day/
- [ ] **Collation:** A collate function combines samples into a batch and handles structures the default stack cannot combine.
  - Example: Batch two variable-length sequences with lengths three and five using a custom collate function.
  - Videos:
    - [PyTorch for deep learning — full course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V_xro1bcAuA) · freeCodeCamp · Daniel Bourke · Long course · approximately 26h
      - Explains: Tensors, training workflows, classification, computer vision and model experiments.
      - Useful because: A long hands-on course: study the relevant workflow, then build a small CPU lab.
      - Watch for: Focus on collation. Then reproduce the lesson example: Batch two variable-length sequences with lengths three and five using a custom collate function.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/learn-pytorch-for-deep-learning-in-day/
- [ ] **Padding masks:** Padding makes shapes rectangular but padded positions must not contribute to attention or token losses.
  - Example: Pad labels with an ignore index and verify additional padding does not change the valid-token average loss.
  - Videos:
    - [PyTorch for deep learning — full course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V_xro1bcAuA) · freeCodeCamp · Daniel Bourke · Long course · approximately 26h
      - Explains: Tensors, training workflows, classification, computer vision and model experiments.
      - Useful because: A long hands-on course: study the relevant workflow, then build a small CPU lab.
      - Watch for: Focus on padding masks. Then reproduce the lesson example: Pad labels with an ignore index and verify additional padding does not change the valid-token average loss.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/learn-pytorch-for-deep-learning-in-day/
- [ ] **Sampling and shuffling:** Training shuffles can reduce order effects; validation must preserve the intended grouping or time boundary.
  - Example: Keep all examples from one person in one split even when a DataLoader shuffles training samples.
  - Videos:
    - [PyTorch for deep learning — full course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V_xro1bcAuA) · freeCodeCamp · Daniel Bourke · Long course · approximately 26h
      - Explains: Tensors, training workflows, classification, computer vision and model experiments.
      - Useful because: A long hands-on course: study the relevant workflow, then build a small CPU lab.
      - Watch for: Focus on sampling and shuffling. Then reproduce the lesson example: Keep all examples from one person in one split even when a DataLoader shuffles training samples.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/learn-pytorch-for-deep-learning-in-day/
- [ ] **Workers and reproducibility:** Worker count changes data loading parallelism and can change randomness; measure before increasing it.
  - Example: Start with num_workers=0 on CPU, seed transforms and compare two identical runs.
  - Videos:
    - [PyTorch for deep learning — full course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V_xro1bcAuA) · freeCodeCamp · Daniel Bourke · Long course · approximately 26h
      - Explains: Tensors, training workflows, classification, computer vision and model experiments.
      - Useful because: A long hands-on course: study the relevant workflow, then build a small CPU lab.
      - Watch for: Focus on workers and reproducibility. Then reproduce the lesson example: Start with num_workers=0 on CPU, seed transforms and compare two identical runs.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.

### SGD, Adam bias correction and decoupled weight decay

Understand optimiser updates well enough to distinguish a learning-rate problem from a regularisation problem.

**Priority:** Useful next · **Study:** 3h · **Practice:** 4h

**Prerequisites:** [SGD, momentum, RMSprop, Adam and AdamW](dl.md#dl-optimizers) Navigation is unrestricted.

#### Concepts

- [ ] **SGD update:** SGD moves opposite an estimated gradient; batch noise and learning rate jointly affect the update.
  - Example: For w=2, gradient=3 and learning rate=0.1, calculate the next weight as 1.7.
  - Videos:
    - [Adam optimization algorithm](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JXQT_vxqwIs) · DeepLearning.AI · Andrew Ng · Focused lecture
      - Explains: First/second moment estimates, bias correction and Adam updates.
      - Useful because: Work through the optimizer state before comparing Adam with SGD.
      - Watch for: Focus on sgd update. Then reproduce the lesson example: For w=2, gradient=3 and learning rate=0.1, calculate the next weight as 1.7.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JXQT_vxqwIs
    - [PyTorch for deep learning — full course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V_xro1bcAuA) · freeCodeCamp · Daniel Bourke · Long course · approximately 26h
      - Explains: Tensors, training workflows, classification, computer vision and model experiments.
      - Useful because: A long hands-on course: study the relevant workflow, then build a small CPU lab.
      - Watch for: Focus on sgd update. Then reproduce the lesson example: For w=2, gradient=3 and learning rate=0.1, calculate the next weight as 1.7.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/learn-pytorch-for-deep-learning-in-day/
- [ ] **Momentum state:** Momentum keeps an exponentially smoothed update direction instead of using only the current gradient.
  - Example: Apply alternating gradients +1 and -1 and compare the momentum trajectory with plain SGD.
  - Videos:
    - [Adam optimization algorithm](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JXQT_vxqwIs) · DeepLearning.AI · Andrew Ng · Focused lecture
      - Explains: First/second moment estimates, bias correction and Adam updates.
      - Useful because: Work through the optimizer state before comparing Adam with SGD.
      - Watch for: Focus on momentum state. Then reproduce the lesson example: Apply alternating gradients +1 and -1 and compare the momentum trajectory with plain SGD.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JXQT_vxqwIs
    - [PyTorch for deep learning — full course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V_xro1bcAuA) · freeCodeCamp · Daniel Bourke · Long course · approximately 26h
      - Explains: Tensors, training workflows, classification, computer vision and model experiments.
      - Useful because: A long hands-on course: study the relevant workflow, then build a small CPU lab.
      - Watch for: Focus on momentum state. Then reproduce the lesson example: Apply alternating gradients +1 and -1 and compare the momentum trajectory with plain SGD.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/learn-pytorch-for-deep-learning-in-day/
- [ ] **Adam first and second moments:** Adam tracks moving estimates of gradients and squared gradients to rescale updates per parameter.
  - Example: Track m and v for three scalar gradients and print the adaptive denominator.
  - Videos:
    - [Adam optimization algorithm](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JXQT_vxqwIs) · DeepLearning.AI · Andrew Ng · Focused lecture
      - Explains: First/second moment estimates, bias correction and Adam updates.
      - Useful because: Work through the optimizer state before comparing Adam with SGD.
      - Watch for: Focus on adam first and second moments. Then reproduce the lesson example: Track m and v for three scalar gradients and print the adaptive denominator.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JXQT_vxqwIs
    - [PyTorch for deep learning — full course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V_xro1bcAuA) · freeCodeCamp · Daniel Bourke · Long course · approximately 26h
      - Explains: Tensors, training workflows, classification, computer vision and model experiments.
      - Useful because: A long hands-on course: study the relevant workflow, then build a small CPU lab.
      - Watch for: Focus on adam first and second moments. Then reproduce the lesson example: Track m and v for three scalar gradients and print the adaptive denominator.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/learn-pytorch-for-deep-learning-in-day/
- [ ] **Bias correction and epsilon:** Moment estimates start at zero; bias correction adjusts early steps and epsilon stabilises division.
  - Example: Compute m/(1-beta1^t) and v/(1-beta2^t) for the first update.
  - Videos:
    - [Adam optimization algorithm](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JXQT_vxqwIs) · DeepLearning.AI · Andrew Ng · Focused lecture
      - Explains: First/second moment estimates, bias correction and Adam updates.
      - Useful because: Work through the optimizer state before comparing Adam with SGD.
      - Watch for: Focus on bias correction and epsilon. Then reproduce the lesson example: Compute m/(1-beta1^t) and v/(1-beta2^t) for the first update.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JXQT_vxqwIs
    - [PyTorch for deep learning — full course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V_xro1bcAuA) · freeCodeCamp · Daniel Bourke · Long course · approximately 26h
      - Explains: Tensors, training workflows, classification, computer vision and model experiments.
      - Useful because: A long hands-on course: study the relevant workflow, then build a small CPU lab.
      - Watch for: Focus on bias correction and epsilon. Then reproduce the lesson example: Compute m/(1-beta1^t) and v/(1-beta2^t) for the first update.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/learn-pytorch-for-deep-learning-in-day/
- [ ] **AdamW versus L2 penalty:** AdamW applies decoupled parameter shrinkage; adding L2 to a loss interacts differently with adaptive rescaling.
  - Example: Compare explicit shrinkage w*(1-lr*decay) against adding decay*w into an Adam gradient.
  - Videos:
    - [Adam optimization algorithm](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JXQT_vxqwIs) · DeepLearning.AI · Andrew Ng · Focused lecture
      - Explains: First/second moment estimates, bias correction and Adam updates.
      - Useful because: Work through the optimizer state before comparing Adam with SGD.

      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.

      - Explains: Tensors, training workflows, classification, computer vision and model experiments.

### Learning-rate schedules, effective batch size and experiments

Tune a training run with controlled evidence rather than changing several settings simultaneously.

**Priority:** Useful next · **Study:** 3h · **Practice:** 4h

**Prerequisites:** [Learning rates, schedules, batch sizes and initialization](dl.md#dl-training-settings) Navigation is unrestricted.

#### Concepts

- [ ] **Warmup:** A warmup increases the learning rate during an initial period; its usefulness depends on model and optimiser rather than a universal rule.
  - Example: Compare a short linear warmup with a fixed rate on the same seeded toy experiment.
  - Videos:
    - [Improving deep neural networks — complete course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hAbRGXkpTX8) · DeepLearning.AI · Andrew Ng · Full course
      - Explains: Initialization, regularization, gradient checking, optimizers and hyperparameter choices.
      - Useful because: A structured theory companion for optimization and training stability.
      - Watch for: Focus on warmup. Then reproduce the lesson example: Compare a short linear warmup with a fixed rate on the same seeded toy experiment.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hAbRGXkpTX8
    - [PyTorch for deep learning — full course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V_xro1bcAuA) · freeCodeCamp · Daniel Bourke · Long course · approximately 26h
      - Explains: Tensors, training workflows, classification, computer vision and model experiments.
      - Useful because: A long hands-on course: study the relevant workflow, then build a small CPU lab.
      - Watch for: Focus on warmup. Then reproduce the lesson example: Compare a short linear warmup with a fixed rate on the same seeded toy experiment.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/learn-pytorch-for-deep-learning-in-day/
- [ ] **Decay schedules:** Step and cosine schedules change learning rate over training and must be stepped at their intended frequency.
  - Example: Plot the learning rate at every optimiser update and detect an accidental per-batch step of an epoch scheduler.
  - Videos:
    - [Improving deep neural networks — complete course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hAbRGXkpTX8) · DeepLearning.AI · Andrew Ng · Full course
      - Explains: Initialization, regularization, gradient checking, optimizers and hyperparameter choices.
      - Useful because: A structured theory companion for optimization and training stability.
      - Watch for: Focus on decay schedules. Then reproduce the lesson example: Plot the learning rate at every optimiser update and detect an accidental per-batch step of an epoch scheduler.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hAbRGXkpTX8
    - [PyTorch for deep learning — full course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V_xro1bcAuA) · freeCodeCamp · Daniel Bourke · Long course · approximately 26h
      - Explains: Tensors, training workflows, classification, computer vision and model experiments.
      - Useful because: A long hands-on course: study the relevant workflow, then build a small CPU lab.
      - Watch for: Focus on decay schedules. Then reproduce the lesson example: Plot the learning rate at every optimiser update and detect an accidental per-batch step of an epoch scheduler.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/learn-pytorch-for-deep-learning-in-day/
- [ ] **Gradient accumulation:** Several microbatches can contribute to one optimiser step, approximating a larger batch when loss scaling is correct.
  - Example: Divide each equally sized microbatch mean loss by the accumulation count and call step only after accumulation.
  - Videos:
    - [Improving deep neural networks — complete course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hAbRGXkpTX8) · DeepLearning.AI · Andrew Ng · Full course
      - Explains: Initialization, regularization, gradient checking, optimizers and hyperparameter choices.
      - Useful because: A structured theory companion for optimization and training stability.
      - Watch for: Focus on gradient accumulation. Then reproduce the lesson example: Divide each equally sized microbatch mean loss by the accumulation count and call step only after accumulation.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hAbRGXkpTX8
    - [PyTorch for deep learning — full course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V_xro1bcAuA) · freeCodeCamp · Daniel Bourke · Long course · approximately 26h
      - Explains: Tensors, training workflows, classification, computer vision and model experiments.
      - Useful because: A long hands-on course: study the relevant workflow, then build a small CPU lab.
      - Watch for: Focus on gradient accumulation. Then reproduce the lesson example: Divide each equally sized microbatch mean loss by the accumulation count and call step only after accumulation.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/learn-pytorch-for-deep-learning-in-day/
- [ ] **Effective batch caveats:** Accumulation is not always identical to one larger batch because batch statistics and unequal final batches can differ.
  - Example: Explain why BatchNorm observes microbatches and weight a short final microbatch by its sample count.
  - Videos:

### BatchNorm, LayerNorm, dropout and train/eval modes

Avoid predictions that change unexpectedly because normalisation or dropout stayed in training mode.

**Priority:** Useful next · **Study:** 3h · **Practice:** 4h

**Prerequisites:** [Dropout, normalization, clipping and early stopping](dl.md#dl-regularization) Navigation is unrestricted.

#### Concepts

- [ ] **Batch normalisation statistics:** BatchNorm normalises features using batch statistics during training and usually running estimates during evaluation.
  - Example: Run the same sample with two different training batches and compare its normalised value.
  - Videos:
    - [Makemore: activations, gradients and BatchNorm](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=P6sfmUTpUmc) · Andrej Karpathy · From-scratch lecture
      - Explains: Activation statistics, initialization problems, gradients and batch normalization.
      - Useful because: Debug vanishing/exploding behavior with measured statistics.
      - Watch for: Focus on batch normalisation statistics. Then reproduce the lesson example: Run the same sample with two different training batches and compare its normalised value.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://karpathy.ai/zero-to-hero.html
    - [PyTorch for deep learning — full course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V_xro1bcAuA) · freeCodeCamp · Daniel Bourke · Long course · approximately 26h
      - Explains: Tensors, training workflows, classification, computer vision and model experiments.
      - Useful because: A long hands-on course: study the relevant workflow, then build a small CPU lab.
      - Watch for: Focus on batch normalisation statistics. Then reproduce the lesson example: Run the same sample with two different training batches and compare its normalised value.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/learn-pytorch-for-deep-learning-in-day/
- [ ] **Layer normalisation axes:** LayerNorm normalises specified trailing dimensions within each example, so its behaviour differs from batch normalisation.
  - Example: Normalise the last D features of a B,T,D tensor and inspect per-token means.
  - Videos:
    - [Makemore: activations, gradients and BatchNorm](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=P6sfmUTpUmc) · Andrej Karpathy · From-scratch lecture
      - Explains: Activation statistics, initialization problems, gradients and batch normalization.
      - Useful because: Debug vanishing/exploding behavior with measured statistics.

      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.

    - [PyTorch for deep learning — full course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V_xro1bcAuA) · freeCodeCamp · Daniel Bourke · Long course · approximately 26h

      - Verification source: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/learn-pytorch-for-deep-learning-in-day/
- [ ] **Dropout scaling:** Training randomly drops activations and scales retained values so the expected output matches the unmasked value.
  - Example: Estimate the average of repeated dropout outputs and compare evaluation output with the original input.
  - Videos:
    - [Makemore: activations, gradients and BatchNorm](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=P6sfmUTpUmc) · Andrej Karpathy · From-scratch lecture
      - Explains: Activation statistics, initialization problems, gradients and batch normalization.
      - Useful because: Debug vanishing/exploding behavior with measured statistics.
      - Watch for: Focus on dropout scaling. Then reproduce the lesson example: Estimate the average of repeated dropout outputs and compare evaluation output with the original input.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.

    - [PyTorch for deep learning — full course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V_xro1bcAuA) · freeCodeCamp · Daniel Bourke · Long course · approximately 26h
      - Explains: Tensors, training workflows, classification, computer vision and model experiments.
      - Useful because: A long hands-on course: study the relevant workflow, then build a small CPU lab.
      - Watch for: Focus on dropout scaling. Then reproduce the lesson example: Estimate the average of repeated dropout outputs and compare evaluation output with the original input.

      - Verification source: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/learn-pytorch-for-deep-learning-in-day/
- [ ] **Evaluation mode versus gradient mode:** model.eval changes modules such as dropout and BatchNorm, while inference_mode controls gradient bookkeeping.
  - Example: Show that no_grad with a training-mode dropout model still produces random predictions.
  - Videos:
